HEADLINE: Disclosure under Reg.30- Order passed by NCLT, Mumbai Bench, in relation to to extension of time for convening the AGM of RCOM for F.Y. 2025-26
summary:
- **NCLT Order (16 Oct 2026)** – The National Company Law Tribunal directed the Registrar of Companies to process Reliance Communications Ltd.’s physical application (dated 1 Sept 2026) for an extension of time to convene the FY 2025‑26 Annual General Meeting, and to allow similar processing for other statutory forms (DPT‑3, MSME‑1, IEPF‑5) that could not be filed electronically because the company is “Under CIRP”.  

- **Compliance Relief** – The Tribunal ordered that no coercive or penal action under Section 99 of the Companies Act, 2013 be taken against the company or its resolution professional for delays caused by the portal limitation, and instructed the MCA to examine such difficulties for CIRP‑affected companies.

rows.Details: National Company Law Tribunal, Mumbai Bench (NCLT).

rows.Particulars: Nature and details of the action (s) taken, or order (s) passed
rows.Details: The Hon’ble NCLT, vide its order dated October 16, 2026, allowed the application filed by the Resolution Professional of Reliance Communications Limited (“Company”), directing the Registrar of Companies, Mumbai-II, to process the Company’s application for extension of time to convene the AGM for FY 2025–26, either physically or through the backend of the MCA portal. The directions also cover other statutory forms affected by the Company’s “Under CIRP” status. Further, no coercive or penal action shall be taken against the Company or the Resolution Professional for delays attributable to the portal-related impediment during the pendency of the proceedings.

rows.Particulars: Date of receipt of direction or order, including any ad-interim or interim orders, or any other communication from the authority
rows.Details: Date of receipt of Order : October 23 2026

rows.Particulars: Details of the violation(s)/contravention(s) committed or alleged to be committed
rows.Details: No specific violation or contravention has been determined against the Company in the aforesaid order. The proceedings concern difficulties in filing the requisite statutory forms on the MCA portal due to the Company’s status as “Under CIRP”.

rows.Particulars: Impact on financial, operation or other activities of the listed entity, quantifiable in monetary terms to the extent possible
rows.Details: The financial impact, if any, is presently not quantifiable. The extension of time for convening and holding the AGM remains subject to processing of the application by the Registrar of Companies in accordance with the order.
